localChanges: Setting up a new game now has a Rules section. The first rule in it is "Units go obsolete": switch it off and a city can go on building Phalanxes after Gunpowder, Triremes after Navigation, and so on for each unit that would have gone obsolete (closes #158).
In a game started without it, the Civilopedia no longer says which advance makes a unit obsolete, or what replaces it.
The choice is kept in a saved game, and the game is played the same way when you load it.

log: Units going obsolete is now a rule set, so a new game will be able to switch it off and go on building Phalanxes after Gunpowder (civ-clone/web-renderer#158).
A game now holds its rule sets, the named groups of rules a new game will be able to switch on or off (civ-clone/web-renderer#158).
A game can now have named groups of rules that are switched on or off together, ready for a new game to offer them as options (civ-clone/web-renderer#158).

A group can hold other groups, so switching a parent switches everything beneath it, and a parent whose children differ says so. A group can also be a choice between alternatives, where exactly one is in force.
A game put together from rules that already had rule sets now gets those same sets, so a saved game's choices can't be lost by being read into an empty set beside them (civ-clone/web-renderer#158).
A saved game now records which rule sets it was started with, and comes back under the same ones when it is loaded (civ-clone/web-renderer#158).
